name: Hawk Dash
summary: Hawk Dash, 25 October: wheel budget moved into the body. The four LOD0 wheels fall from 668 to 176 triangles (74% less), with five-spoke rims drawn in the shared atlas and closed inner sidewalls at every tier. The body now has tucked sills and fuller flanks, rolled shoulders, a crowned bonnet and shaped power bulge, a rounded roof and bowed windscreen/backlight, a wider lower intake, contoured bumper and recessed boot panel. The diffuser, fins and wing tips are closed. The existing collision hulls and handling are retained. The labelled reference / before / after / diff sheets below show the change in the same blue paint and lighting. This is a review candidate; the owner judges the likeness.
feedback: Comment on this page (what to change, which view or state); the session turns each comment into a bug bead that cites this page and the car's id.

specTwin.sharedSpec: One spec, two bodies (R123): the Hawk Dash and the Lion President name spec 'aussie-v8' in web/shared/src/roster.json, and their profiles' handling (tuning) is identical, held by tools/vehicles/test/spec-twins.test.mjs. Rear drive, 1700 kg, Cruz-like launch, more power per kilo for a higher top speed; the bodies (hull, wheels, damage parts) are each car's own.

findings.text: source/contract/reproducibility: bake.txt, reproducibility.txt (`node tools/vehicles/bake.mjs art/vehicles/hawk-dash --check`), contract.txt (`jj vehicle sync` and `jj validate`), no waivers.

geometry/budget: verify.mjs checks the shipped GLBs, all 11 part IDs, finite vertices/normals, nonzero triangles, one material and sealed manifold wheels at all tiers. Wheel bottoms meet ground and wheel pivots match sidecar. geometry.json records per-part counts.

paint and hinges: `node --test tools/vehicles/test/{pivots,paint-key,spec-twins}.test.mjs`, 42 passed (paint-spec-tests.txt). Bright/white/near-black paint keeps tyres, rims, lamps and framed glass neutral (paints.png, paints-strip.png).

damage geometry: damage-strip.png and damage-strip-overview.png show intact, loose, detached and stripped-shell poses with dark bays. This is the existing evidence viewer, not a new simulation test of debris lifetime; no damage runtime code changed.

physics fit: final-sim.json, `jj sim --json --profile assets/profiles/hawk-dash.json settle.json scenarios/handling/roster-straight-hawk-dash.json`, both fixtures pass and replay matches. The focused settle fixture reuses the original idle-settle drops and settle checks verbatim. Original Cruz idle-settle asks for at least 2° pitch; Hawk reaches 1.6967° before and after and fails those two Cruz-specific checks identically (sim.json, physics-before-after.json). All other checks pass; before/after state hashes are identical. No fixture was relaxed to claim a handling improvement.

visual inspection: views.png, lods.png, colliders.png, all three comparison sheets, damage and paint strips, grid-1/4/24.png. These grids use the model evidence viewer. Current roof-number anchor was raised to clear the new crown. Runtime identity and N×N draw benchmarks were not rerun because host loader/material/batching are unchanged; the grids do not prove roof-number readability. review-probe.mjs exercises all three LODs, three seat paints and intact/loose/detached states through the actual POC controls in Chromium and WebKit; screenshots and checks.json are in local-interactions/ and live-interactions/.

engine gate: the unchanged Hawk sound profile passes schema validation (engine.txt P7). The broad sound-lab check reports seven failures: M5/B12/L6 squeal, B10/L1 firing pitch, K2 start and SL1 control inventory. These are outside this geometry change; tracked with br-8h3u.12. No sound files changed. This report does not certify the sound lab.
